html:
Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia, on the Kura River, founded according to legend by King Vakhtang Gorgasali of Iberia in the late 400s and made the capital by his son Dachi in the early 500s.

The story says the king's falcon fell into a hot spring there, and the name means warm place. The city lay on trade routes between Persia, the steppe and the Black Sea and was taken by Persians, Arabs, Byzantines, Seljuks and Mongols. Arab emirs ruled it for four centuries until David the Builder retook it in 1122 and made it the royal capital. The Persian shah Agha Mohammad Khan sacked it in 1795. Under Russia it was the capital of the whole Caucasus, with large Armenian and Persian quarters.
